# SOMOSGAY (Somosgay) — Online Research Dossier

**What follows is a deep dive into every meaningful public footprint I could pull in ▉

one session.** FYI, this is a personal-org/activist group, not a business — so I'll skip the "business analysis" lens and use a research/NGO profile instead. Sources are inline hyperlinks; I quote the language people actually used because tone matters here.

---

*TL;DR*

SOMOSGAY is the leading LGBTQ+ rights NGO in Paraguay. Founded 2009 by *Simón Cazal* in Asunción. Runs a community centre + drop-in space, the country's first dedicated LGBT men's health/HIV clinic (*Kuimba'e*, 2013), a youth shelter ~40 minutes outside the capital, and (since ~2017) the *AMI* app for HIV testing, appointments and discrimination reporting. Backed historically by amfAR, UNAIDS, AIDS Healthcare Foundation, Fundación Triángulo (Spain), All Out. Currently active on GlobalGiving/Benevity. Strategy mixes HIV services, PrEP/PEP advocacy, marriage equality litigation, religious-engagement (Cazal met Pope Francis in 2015), and Pride mobilisations. Climate: hostile — five consecutive conservative governments since founding, current president Santiago Peña openly hostile; marriage equality rejected in court in 2013 and still off the table.

---

*1. Identity snapshot*

| | |
|---|---|
| Full name | SOMOSGAY ("Somosgay", "We Are Gay") |
| Type | LGBTQ+ advocacy + service NGO |
| Founded | 2009, Asunción, Paraguay |
| Co-founder / Executive Director | Simón Cazal Fernández |
| Co-founder / partner activist | Sergio López |
| HQ / centre | Asunción (historical address: *Independencia Nacional 1032 casi Manduvirá*) |
| Sister/sibling org | *AIREANA* — Paraguay's first lesbian org, founded later; both active in joint Pride and joint advocacy |
| Site | https://www.somosgay.org · https://www.facebook.com/somosgayasuncion |
| Mission (own words) | "Contribuir en la atención al VIH, innovar con estrategias efectivas contra la LGBTIfobia, y promover la defensa de los derechos humanos" |

---

*2. Founder — Simón Cazal*

- Born 1980 in Villeta, Paraguay. Openly atheist — a notable fact in deeply Catholic Paraguay, and the basis for the surreal anecdote below.
- 2009: co-signs agreement with the Ministry of Interior to "eradicate homophobia" within the National Police (early, pragmatic track).
- *23 March 2012:* marries Sergio López in Rosario, Argentina — first foreign same-sex couple to marry there under Argentina's 2010 law.
- *2013:* their bid to have the marriage recognised in Paraguay is refused by Civil & Commercial judge *Nery Kunzle* on constitutional grounds.
- *2015:* invited (by the Paraguayan Bishops' Conference itself!) to the civil-society roundtable with *Pope Francis* during his Paraguay visit, alongside 1,600 other civil-society leaders. Says the meeting was "very productive." Pope "highlighted diversity." He's believed to be the first openly married gay activist to meet a sitting Pope in a public forum.
- *2024 (ABC Color):* still leading the org, framing Paraguay as "the only state in the region that openly treats LGBT people as second-class citizens," and characterising the state as "stronista, castrense, heteropatriarcal" (i.e., continuity of the Stroessner-era authoritarian mould).
- Wikipedia ES page on him: https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim%C3%B3n_Cazal
- Press portraits: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/jul/10/simon-cazal-pope-francis-paraguay-lgbt-somosgay · https://edition.cnn.com/2015/07/11/world/lgbt-paraguay-pope-francis/index.html · https://www.advocate.com/politics/religion/2015/07/12/married-gay-activist-s-meeting-pope-was-very-productive · https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2024/06/28/derechos-lgbt-en-paraguay-matrimonio-igualitario-a-la-vista/

---

*3. What they actually run*

*3.1 Community centre (Asunción)*
Drop-in space + cultural events + workshops. Visitors describe it as "colourfully decorated, well appointed." Houses:
- Free HIV testing
- Counseling
- Job trainings
- Psychological support
- Safe space for LGBT youth and people living with HIV

*3.2 *Kuimba'e* Men's Health Clinic (2013 — Asunción)*
- *Paraguay's first dedicated men's health clinic*, opened May 2013.
- "Kuimba'e" = Guaraní for "men."
- Free rapid HIV testing.
- Specialist referrals for anal/rectal health (proctology).
- Goals: expand voluntary testing, link to anti-HIV treatment, run campaigns.
- Backed by: *amfAR (GMT initiative), AIDS Healthcare Foundation (LA), UNAIDS Southern Cone, Fundación Triángulo (Spain).*
- Source: https://www.washingtonblade.com/2012/12/10/lgbt-group-hopes-to-open-paraguays-first-mens-health-clinic/

*3.3 Youth shelter (outside Asunción)*
Rehabilitated abandoned country house ~40 min from the city. Capacity when visited: 5 teens + chaperone. Architecture: courtyard with a fountain decorated in 108 rainbow tiles, support columns painted rainbow. The "108" is a deliberate reference (see §6). Chosen because trans/LGBT teens are routinely thrown out of family homes.

*3.4 *AMI* App (recent, ~2022+)*
Per their own site copy (https://www.somosgay.org/noticias/detalles/asuntos):
- HIV-services orchestration
- Discrimination/LGBTIfobia reporting
- Job-board for the community
- Access to kits, testing, clinic appointments
- Stated approach: combination prevention + PrEP/PEP + adherence-to-treatment → undetectable viral load for all who test positive → end HIV as a public-health problem in Paraguay.

*3.5 Pragmatic police-LGBT agreement (2009)*
Early win: signed cooperation with the Ministry of Interior to push homophobia out of the National Police. Symbolic but rare in the region.

*3.6 Public campaigns / annual events*
- *Marcha del Orgullo* (Pride) in Asunción — annual; co-organised with AIREANA. Cazal told ABC in 2024 that the march keeps growing year-over-year.
- *Besatón (kiss-in)* in the public square in front of Parliament — annual.
- 108-themed symbolism woven through publications, the shelter fountain, and political messaging.

---

*5. Political context — *why* this organisation exists*

This is the lens that makes everything else legible. Paraguay is the *only country in South America with no civil marriage equality* (as of 2024–2025 reporting), and has had five consecutive conservative governments since SOMOSGAY was founded in 2009.

- *Constitutional text* explicitly names and protects "marriage" between a man and a woman — frames anti-LGBT legislation as applying the constitution rather than violating it.

- *The "108" scar:* in 1959, under Stroessner's dictatorship, police raided homes on the pretext of an unsolved murder of a radio personality, arrested and tortured 108 alleged gay men. The number is now iconic in Paraguay's LGBT movement — both a mark of shame (people change addresses/plates to avoid it) and a badge of identity for the community. SOMOSGAY codes "108" into its visual identity.
- *Religious capture:* unlike neighbours, Paraguay's constitution doesn't name a state religion, but in practice Catholic/evangelical clergy have dominant access to broadcast media. Politicians regularly recycle the US-style "paedophilia / recruitment / biblical" playbook against LGBT protections. No accountability on those statements.
- *2017 wave (Cartes government):*
  - 5 Oct 2017 — Ministry of Education resolution *N° 29664*: bans any "gender ideology" or "non-traditional family" teaching materials in public schools.
  - President *Horacio Cartes* publicly apologised for "contradictions" within his ministries and aligned with "pro-family" groups.
  - "KKK Paraguay" Facebook page publicly thanked Cartes.
  - Senators introduced a "bill for the integral protection of the family" explicitly defining family through "procreation."
  - Gay Times piece in Dec 2017 (Ana Andrade, All Out) was the trigger for the international second-shelter fundraising campaign.
- *2024 (Peña government):* Cazal told ABC Color that openly homophobic statements now come from the President himself and from media aligned with the government. The framing: "the same political clans that ran the dictatorship are still running the show; the dictatorship ended legally, but the political class didn't."

Sources: https://www.gaytimes.com/life/anti-lgbtq-hate-in-paraguay/ · https://www.ibanet.org/article/3263508E-230C-4B0C-8DD5-6CCB9D203774 · https://www.latimes.com/espanol/internacional/articulo/2024-09-03/los-condones-no-son-confiables-en-el-1er-programa-de-educacion-sexual-del-paraguay-catolico

---

*6. Marriage equality — Cazal & López's strategic role*

This deserves its own section because it's the org's most concrete legal-political play, and it's been running for 12+ years.

- *2010-03-23* — Cazal's famous "Hasta el matrimonio no paramos" ("We won't stop until marriage") declaration to Paraguayan press. He framed the wedding he'd seek in Argentina as the opening move.
- *2012-03-23* — married Sergio López in Rosario, Argentina. First foreign same-sex couple to marry under Argentina's 2010 law.
- *2013-03-22* — filed formal petition in Asunción to register the marriage in Paraguay.
- *2013-04-04* — Civil & Commercial judge *Nery Kunzle* refuses: holds that the Paraguayan constitution doesn't permit same-sex marriage.
- *2022-03* — Cazal and López publicly mark 10 years since that marriage, file additional appeals.
- *2024* — still the same constitutional constraint. Marriage equality remains distant. Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Colombia, Chile (2022) all out; Paraguay is the regional holdout. CIDH 2018 ruling that family ties can derive from same-sex relationships is on the books but ignored.
- *2025* — no change in legal status; inequality strategically framed as "the constitution protects marriage between a man and a woman" by the state.

Takeaway: their litigation strategy since 2012 hasn't worked tactically — but it has built the legal foundation + public record for any future IACHR challenge and keeps the issue in national press.

---

*7. Sister org — AIREANA*

Often co-mentioned. AIREANA is Paraguay's first lesbian organisation and hosts annual events like the LGBT film festival (running since ~2009–2010, 15th edition reported by IBA). Sister org relationship runs deep:
- Co-organise Pride.
- Joint use of staff/volunteers (the IBA article describes the same Simón Cazal visit where volunteers from both orgs hosted him).
- Shared digital audience — their Facebook and Instagram overlap heavily.

Per https://www.ibanet.org/article/3263508E-230C-4B0C-8DD5-6CCB9D203774, Rosa Posa, AIREANA volunteer, the response to "do you need pity?": *"Don't be pitiful — people here and NGOs are working in spite of society. This is a grassroots operation. People will be ready."*
